data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The durable binding that alone turns silent divergence between a published result and its replayed log into a contradiction is **cryptographic commitment to the log's entire state at publication time**, ensuring that any retroactive alteration is detectable as a violation of the commitment.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The commitment scheme must be collision-resistant; otherwise, an attacker could generate a divergent log with the same commitment.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log's state at publication time must be fully captured in the commitment (e.g., no hidden state or external dependencies).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The replay mechanism must be deterministic or include all non-deterministic elements (e.g., timestamps, random seeds) in the commitment.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The commitment must be published in a tamper-evident medium (e.g., blockchain, public timestamping service) to prevent retroactive alteration of the commitment itself.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A cryptographic commitment (e.g., Merkle root or hash chain) binds the log's state at publication time to a fixed, verifiable representation. If the replayed log diverges from this representation, the divergence is detectable as a cryptographic inconsistency, making silent divergence a contradiction (i.e., the log cannot simultaneously match the commitment and diverge from it).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
